Hi Alex,

Thanks for the call last week. Attached is the Montclare procurement questionnaire focused on site eligibility and cross-border processing constraints. We need to confirm the following at a minimum so we can clear your platform with our legal and data governance teams: 1) Whether customer data (requests and model input) and derived artifacts (embeddings, KV cache, logs) can be restricted to EU-only physical locations; 2) Fallback behavior (if EU capacity is unavailable, do we fail open to US/APAC or queue requests); 3) Telemetry/PII contained in logs and retention defaults; 4) KMS and key locality — can keys be tied to EU-only key stores; 5) Any parts of processing that transit through US-based control planes or telemetry endpoints.

We prefer short, specific answers in the spreadsheet (column per question) and any supporting operational playbook. Our target deadline for an initial response is COB Thursday to review internally the following week.

Alex / Laura —

Attached is a draft answer set (Site-Eligibility-Answers-v1.docx) and inline key points below so Alex can assemble. I focused on encryption, logs, telemetry, and key locality. Please mark edits inline in the doc; I will incorporate.

Summary of draft answers (high level):
- Data plane locality: For Hosted customers we run customer workloads in region-specific clusters (EU/US/APAC) and can restrict model inference and persistent storage to EU regions for data-at-rest. For higher assurance we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated pools where tenant isolation and region pinning can be contractually committed.

- Fallback behavior: Default hosted policy: region-aware routing with automatic soft-fallback to nearest compatible region during transient capacity events (this is configurable). We can disable automatic cross-region failover for contractual customers and instead queue or return 429s when EU capacity is exhausted. Dedicated/Private deployments allow absolute region-only operation (no cross-region fallback).

- KMS / key locality: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. Customers can bring keys in AWS KMS (EU regions), GCP KMS (EU regions), or use HSM-backed key stores. For Hosted offering keys can be scoped to EU KMS; note that some control-plane operations (key orchestration metadata) may traverse our control plane, which is multiregion — we can provide audit logs and contractual assurances. For full EU-only key handling, Private deployment with customer KMS/VPC is recommended.

- Logs & telemetry: Operational logs include request metadata, latency, error codes. We do not store raw model outputs in operational telemetry by default. PII: customers can opt-in to redact or suppress user content in telemetry. Default retention: 30 days for request-level telemetry; enterprise retention (contracted) can be extended (e.g., 7 years) or shortened to 0 days for sensitive customers. We provide mechanisms to export and purge logs on demand.

- Control plane and telemetry endpoints: Our control plane orchestrates routing and scheduling and emits anonymized telemetry. For Hosted customers, control-plane endpoints reside in multiple regions; certain telemetry aggregates may be processed in US-based services. For contractual customers (Dedicated/Private) we can route control plane and telemetry ingress to EU-only endpoints; full air-gapped/no-egress requires Private on-prem deployment.

- Operational playbook (attached): page 3 contains our geo-failover decision tree and activation triggers, page 7 lists the contact points and escalation SLAs.

Open questions for Montclare:
1) Do you require a contractual prohibition on any cross-border fallback, or is a queue/429 acceptable?
2) Do you have a KMS provider preference (AWS/GCP/Azure) for EU keys?
3) Telemetry: do you require deletion/pseudonymization of user content prior to any telemetry export?

Attachments: Site-Eligibility-Answers-v1.docx (docx, 48 KB)

Thanks — Priyom
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Completed: Montclare site eligibility & jurisdictional cutover answers (attached)

Hi Anna / Dan,

Thanks for the patience — attached is our consolidated response to your site-eligibility questionnaire. Highlights:

- EU-only processing: We can operate inference and persistent customer storage in EU regions and can offer Dedicated pools or Private (VPC) deployments for contractual EU-only guarantees. For Hosted customers we can disable automatic cross-region fallback on a per-customer basis (requests will queue or return a 429 when EU capacity is unavailable).

- Keys & encryption: AES-256 at rest; support for customer-managed KMS in EU regions (AWS/GCP/Azure). For full control-plane locality and key handling we recommend Private deployment with customer KMS.

- Telemetry & logs: Default retention 30 days; no raw model outputs are included in operational telemetry by default. We offer telemetry redaction, on-demand log purge, and contractual retention windows.

- Control plane: hosted control plane is multiregion; we can restrict telemetry ingestion to EU endpoints for enterprise customers and provide audit evidence. Air-gapped / no-egress scenarios are addressed by our Private on-prem package.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached PDF (Montclare_SiteEligibility_Answers_20270819.pdf) — it's the consolidated, signed draft.
2) If Montclare needs a binding contract clause (e.g., data residency SLA, cross-border egress prohibition) we can feed this into our legal team and produce redlines.
3) We propose a 45-minute technical review on Tue 24 Aug 2027 to walk the playbook and failover triggers — proposed invite will follow.

Attachments: Montclare_SiteEligibility_Answers_20270819.pdf (pdf, 210 KB); Redwood_Operational_Playbook.pdf (pdf, 1.2 MB)

Best regards,
Alex Martinez
